title: You Must Be CRAZY To Do Pair Programming
summary: Dave Farley makes the case for pair programming: better quality, near-double speed, learning and onboarding, with pair rotation and pairing-by-default advice.

assertions.quote: all of the studies that I've ever seen show this increase in quality
two people are nearly but not quite twice as fast

verdicts.note: Meta-analysis finds pairs cut elapsed time but raise total effort; the sixty-percent figure comes from small student studies.
A survey of 122 IT employees found 73% of those who pair believe it speeds up development; this is perception only and says nothing about total person-hours.

assertions.quote: i know of no better way of spreading learning
they also had much higher confidence in their solutions
it's dumb to waste two people's time on the boring repetitive stuff

verdicts.note: Meta-analysis finds pairing's benefit concentrated on complex tasks, consistent with this.

assertions.quote: i could cure that by having some form of always-on review pair programming
it really doesn't matter very much what the what the combinations are all of them have some value

verdicts.note: Experiments find novice pairs gain most and expert pairs least; all combinations show some benefit.

Student surveys in the review found pairing difficult when there was a large skill differential, with one respondent reporting the pair was unproductive whenever the weaker member was not driving; the review repeats this as a reported limitation.
